tested_scope.candidate: lightweight GitHub REST repository-contents API as scheduled-Chat durable control/evidence transport
tested_scope.claim: A Chat-exposed repository transport can persist and recover small control/evidence artifacts without a Work/protected-primary/manual-user executor, while rate-limit interruptions are handled by durable cross-invocation continuation rather than same-run retry.

verified_points: update requires the current blob sha
concurrent create/update and delete operations can conflict and should be serialized
authenticated requests have a finite request-per-hour limit
on rate-limit errors stop requests until the documented retry/reset condition rather than continuing to retry

exact_chat_repository_evidence.this_invocation_observation: The connected Chat GitHub surface successfully fetched the current note repository control files before this audit write.

findings.reason: Primary sources and exposed Chat capability support the lightweight transport mechanism and its rate-limit-safe lifecycle, but this slice does not prove global zero-cost billing semantics, every candidate route, or all Phase-1 hard gates. Rate limits are a bounded transport interruption to checkpoint across invocations, not evidence of a monthly/trial/paid quota dependency.

continuation: Next primary_source_verifier invocation: verify one exact candidate route's SHA-bound update/CAS and idempotency assumptions against official GitHub Contents API semantics plus current repository evidence, without injecting a conflicting write; preserve the distinction between ordinary request-rate interruption and forbidden finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency, and do not claim Phase-1 acceptance from transport evidence alone.
